body.statement:
For each fixed \(P_0\in\operatorname{int}(\mathcal F_s)\), there are a class-wide constant \(C_1>0\) and center-dependent constants \(c_0(P_0)>0\) and \(\kappa(P_0)>0\) such that
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}\mathbb E_P\lVert\widehat\tau-\tau(P)\rVert^2
\leq C_1\frac{L_n}{n}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\), and
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{n}{L_n}
\inf_{\widetilde\tau_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal N_n(P_0,\kappa(P_0))}
\mathbb E_P\lVert\widetilde\tau_n-\tau(P)\rVert^2
\geq c_0(P_0).
\]
The lower bound is witnessed by def:green-local-alternatives and lem:green-local-alternatives, for which \(\log(1/\varepsilon_n)=(\eta/a_h)L_n\).  The upper bound remains the uniform assertion over \(\mathcal F_s\).
body.justification: The testing reduction gives the lower-rate mechanism, while the upper-risk half requires integrated uniform remainder bounds.
body.gap: Weak convergence and deterministic differentiability do not supply the missing second-moment control.
body.consumer: A matched minimax rate is not yet claimed.

obligation.what_is_open: Prove the class-uniform upper second-moment bound and finish the lower bound after the corrected local alternatives are certified.
obligation.obstruction: The upper risk needs integrated tails for the mixed nonlinear remainder and the fallback event; weak convergence does not provide them.
obligation.attempted: The two-point testing reduction and logarithmic separation arithmetic are complete conditionally on the corrected local-alternative lemma.
obligation.partial_result:
If lem:green-local-alternatives is completed for the corrected derivative, its two alternatives satisfy
\[
\Delta_n^2\geq c(P_0)\zeta^2\frac{L_n}{n}.
\]
The standard nearest-parameter testing reduction and the product-Hellinger bound then yield a positive local lower constant after multiplication by \(n/L_n\).  The class-uniform upper bound remains unproved because it needs integrated control of the mixed nested remainder and of the measurable fallback event; weak convergence alone does not control the required second moment.
